title: Magnetic covalent triazine–Pd nanocomposite as an efficient catalyst for Suzuki C–C cross coupling
content: Herein, we describe the synthesis of a novel nanomagnetic palladium complex based on a nitrogen-rich triazine-based covalent organic polymer (TCOP) immobilized on spinel magnetic nanoparticles. The material was prepared through stepwise surface functionalization of hercynite with cyanuric chloride, followed by in situ polymerization with melamine and subsequent palladium grafting. Comprehensive characterizations confirmed the successful attachment of organic moieties onto the hercynite surface. This modification led to the formation of a sponge-like nanosized shell around the hercynite core, which uniformly immobilized Pd(0) species through coordination with nitrogen groups. The resulting catalyst exhibited high crystallinity as well as excellent thermal and structural stability. The obtained [Hercynite@TCOP-Pd(0)] nanocomposite demonstrated high efficiency in the selective Suzuki coupling of aryl iodides, bromides, and chlorides with phenylboronic acid in PEG-400 as a green solvent, affording excellent yields (up to 98%) within short reaction times. The catalyst was successfully evaluated with various substituted aryl halides bearing both electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups. Recyclability and stability tests showed that the nanocomposite could be reused up to eight times without a noticeable decrease in activity and exhibited low palladium leaching, making it an effective and reliable catalytic system for cross-coupling reactions.
